cards.claim: Optimal learning rate exhibits non-monotonic 'surge' behavior with batch size for Adam-style optimizers, not linear scaling
cards.conditions: Adam-style optimizers using sign of gradients; conditions under Gaussian gradient approximation (Central Limit Theorem)
cards.effect: Optimal LR first rises, reaches peak at batch size B*, then falls as batch size increases further—contradicts previous linear/square-root scaling assumptions
cards.evidence: Theoretical derivation (Theorem 2, Theorem 3, Eq. 2) combined with experimental validation on CNN-FashionMNIST, ResNet18-TinyImageNet, DistilGPT2-ELI5, and MoE-RedPajama
cards.quote: In scenarios involving small batch sizes, the optimal learning rate initially increases and then decreases, resembling a surge in the sea, as depicted by the dashed orange line. For large batch sizes, we identify a value to which the optimal learning rate converges.

cards.claim: Critical batch size B* (where optimal LR peaks) shifts to larger batch sizes as training progresses
cards.conditions: Any Adam-style optimizer training; measured across training progression at different achieved loss levels
cards.effect: The batch size corresponding to peak optimal LR gradually increases as loss decreases during training; affects hyperparameter schedule timing
cards.evidence: Experimental observation across ResNet18-TinyImageNet (Figure 3), explicit statement in theoretical summary: 'the peak value of the surge will gradually move toward the larger batch size as training progresses'
cards.quote: Comparing the red dashed lines in different figures, we can see that the estimated [B*] gradually increases as the training progresses (i.e. training loss decreases), which corroborates the second conclusion in Section 2.3.

cards.claim: Learning rate scaling law differs fundamentally between Adam and SGD: square root vs. linear scaling, respectively
cards.conditions: When batch size B < B*; Gaussian gradient assumption holds
cards.effect: Adam-style optimizers require different LR adjustment rules than SGD when scaling batch size; cannot apply SGD scaling rules (Eq. 3) to Adam (Eq. 4)
cards.evidence: Theoretical (Eq. 2 vs. Eq. 3-4) and validated across multiple workloads showing SGD curves fail to capture Adam's peak
cards.quote: when [B < B*], for SGD, the scaling law of optimal learning rates with batch sizes transitions into linear scaling, consistent with previous conclusions [...] while for Adam, the relationship transitions into square root scaling

cards.claim: Critical batch size B* is simultaneously the peak of optimal learning rate AND the balance point between training speed and data efficiency
cards.conditions: Both SGD and Adam optimizers; valid for all training regimes
cards.effect: B* determines both hyperparameter sensitivity (LR peak) and computational efficiency trade-off; moving beyond B* sacrifices data efficiency for marginal speed gains
cards.evidence: Theorem 5, equations 20-21; conclusion in Section 2.3: 'the batch size that corresponds to the local maximum optimal learning rate is consistent with the balance point of training speed and data efficiency'
cards.quote: In Adam scenarios, [B*] is not only the local maximum of the optimal learning rate, but also the balance point between training speed and data efficiency.

cards.claim: Optimal learning rate converges to a non-zero asymptotic value at very large batch sizes (not zero)
cards.conditions: When batch size B >> B*; Theorem 4 conditions
cards.effect: Even at batch sizes far larger than critical point, LR plateau remains positive; suggests hard floor on LR reduction vs. batch increase
cards.evidence: Theorem 4 (Eq. 17) with proof in Appendix E; Figure 1 schematic showing asymptotic approach to stable non-zero value; discussion in Section 2.3
cards.quote: when B increases infinitely, the optimal learning rate will eventually converge to a non-zero value.

cards.claim: Prior SGD-derived scaling laws fail to predict Adam optimizer behavior at the optimal LR peak
cards.conditions: Comparing previous approximations (cited refs 24, 23) with actual optimal LR measurements; small-to-medium batch sizes
cards.effect: Using SGD rules for Adam hyperparameter scaling can miss the LR peak by up to ~0.5 dB in loss at critical batch sizes; systematic misprediction of optimal LR
cards.evidence: Experimental figures (2-5) showing SGD curve with β=1/8 systematically fails to match observed Adam optimal LRs; ResNet18 (Figure 3) shows SGD approximation 'fails to capture the peak optimal learning rate'
cards.quote: Although the SGD curve with [β=1/8], which is claimed by [24] to represent the Adam optimizer, serves as a good approximation in certain cases, it fails to capture the peak optimal learning rate as our Adam curve does.
